# Michel de Montaigne quote sources

8 passages attributed to Michel de Montaigne in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Montaigne.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Michel de Montaigne

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

French

Cited here from

The Essays (I.20, I.26, I.31, I.39, II.12, III.2, III.13), and the tower motto recorded as cf. II.12.

How to cite it

Book and chapter — Essays I.20 — which is the standard convention and is stable across editions. Where a passage was added after 1588, scholarly editions mark it; say so if the distinction matters to the point you are making.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Montaigne revised the Essays continuously and the posthumous 1595 text contains large additions made after the first two editions, marked in modern editions as layer \[C\]. A sentence may therefore be in the 1580 book or added near the end of his life, which is a real difference in what he had settled on. The tower motto “Que sais-je?” is an inscription, not a line from the Essays, and is flagged here as such.

1 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can I check quotations attributed to Michel de Montaigne?

Book and chapter — Essays I.20 — which is the standard convention and is stable across editions. Where a passage was added after 1588, scholarly editions mark it; say so if the distinction matters to the point you are making. This archive cites Michel de Montaigne from The Essays (I.20, I.26, I.31, I.39, II.12, III.2, III.13), and the tower motto recorded as cf. II.12. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

### What is the most common mistake when quoting Michel de Montaigne?

Montaigne revised the Essays continuously and the posthumous 1595 text contains large additions made after the first two editions, marked in modern editions as layer \[C\]. A sentence may therefore be in the 1580 book or added near the end of his life, which is a real difference in what he had settled on. The tower motto “Que sais-je?” is an inscription, not a line from the Essays, and is flagged here as such.

### What language did Michel de Montaigne write in?

French. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
